models_evaluated: hydronephrosis AI model predicting obstructive hydronephrosis from renal ultrasounds

links.outcome: Change in nuclear scan use after clinicians' exposure to model development and silent trial
links.effect: Nuclear scans fell from 80 to 58% (P=0.005) after the silent trial, with no identifiable change in workflow, personnel, guidelines, or patient characteristics. Authors propose separating clinical end-users in development from those in validation.
links.quote: Model-induced belief revision may threaten the scientific integrity of AI research, because it can lead to underestimated differences between AI predictions and clinical judgment, which may unconsciously be influenced by this phenomenon.

unlisted_practices: Maintain clear boundaries between clinical end-users involved in model development and those involved in validation/silent trial to avoid induced belief revision
Test and mitigate induced belief revision (data-induced and model-induced) in AI research

screen.reason: Empirical case study observing an unintended clinical practice change (induced belief revision) during/after a silent trial of an imaging AI model, but it does not compare outcomes with vs without a specific safeguard or deployment practice.
